strongest_angle: In November 2026, Nature reported that 3.95-billion-year-old rocks found in Hebei, China reveal oceanic crust was buried over 50 kilometers deep in Earth's early history.

key_facts.fact: A research team led by Yusheng Wan at the Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences identified 3.95-billion-year-old rocks in the Shimen Complex in the Jidong region of Hebei Province, China.
A study published in Nature reported that by 3.95 billion years ago, surface-altered oceanic crust was rapidly buried to depths greater than 50 kilometers and partially melted.
The 3.95-billion-year-old rocks from northern China represent the oldest rocks found in Asia and the second-oldest in the world after Canada's 4.0-billion-year-old Acasta Gneiss.
Scientists estimate Earth formed approximately 4.5 billion years ago, but surface rocks older than 3.9 billion years remain exceptionally rare.

quotes.text: Ancient rocks in northern China reveal that by 3.95 billion years ago, surface-altered oceanic crust had been buried rapidly to depths greater than 50 kilometres and partly melted.
